# Opportunity & Context

Partner National Statistical Offices (NSOs) in low- and middle-income countries face severe proprietary licensing costs (SAS, SPSS, Stata) and seek sustainable pathways to modern open-source software (R, Python, Quarto).

The [**Posit Community Support Granting Scheme**](https://opensource.posit.co/about/community-support) provides a low-barrier, unbureaucratic source of funding that partner statistical offices and local user groups can leverage directly to aid their open-source transitions and technical upskilling.

# What Does Posit Fund?

- **Financial Micro-Grants**: Small-to-medium grants averaging **~$1,000 USD** (typically $500–$2,000 USD). Ideal for covering local workshop logistics, training materials, travel stipends, or honoraria for regional guest trainers.
- **Educational & Cloud Infrastructure**: Free access to Posit Cloud / Posit Connect Cloud for training workshops, Positron server licenses for institutional teaching, and AI compute credits.
- **Global Visibility**: Amplification of local events through Posit's international developer network.

# Practical Value for Partner NSOs

Unlike complex multilateral development grants (e.g., EU Twinning, World Bank), Posit’s application is a single, lightweight rolling form requiring zero institutional co-funding. It is ideally suited for local statistical champions seeking to establish internal "R Forums", run hands-on reproducibility bootcamps, or build regional data science communities.

# Suggested Action for DST Consulting

DST experts can recommend this funding mechanism during bilateral advisory missions on statistical modernization and help partner NSO colleagues frame lightweight applications around open statistical workflows.
